Reopen a tutorial with a student's downloaded answers filled in

Source: R/load_tutorial.R
load_tutorial.Rd

Takes the JSON file a reader downloaded with the "Download My Answers" button, works out which tutorial it came from, renders (or reuses the cached render of) that tutorial exactly as run_tutorial() would, and opens it with every answer in the file already submitted, as if the reader had just typed them in. The reader can then carry on, correct what needs correcting, and download a new file. The usual case is a resubmission: a student whose file has one wrong URL fixes that answer instead of redoing the tutorial.

Usage

load_tutorial(
  path,
  output_dir = tools::R_user_dir("learnr2", "cache"),
  open = interactive(),
  refresh = FALSE
)

Arguments

path

Path to a JSON file downloaded with download_answers_button(). It must name its package and tutorial (files downloaded before learnr2 recorded them cannot be loaded); a missing version, or one that differs from the installed package, is reported as a warning, since the tutorial's questions may have changed.

output_dir, open, refresh

As for run_tutorial(). With open = FALSE the tutorial is rendered and the restore page written, but nothing is served or opened; the restore page's path is returned.

Value

The path of the restore page, invisibly.

What is restored

Every entry in the file's answers whose id matches a question() or a {webr} exercise on the rendered page, plus the student_info() form. A choice question gets its picked options back, a text question its text, a reflection its text or pasted screenshot, an exercise its code. Sections are unlocked through the last one holding a restored answer, so the page opens where the reader left off. An entry whose id matches nothing (the tutorial has changed since the download, say) is dropped with a warning naming it. Answers never submitted (null in the file) are left blank.

Answers live in the browser's localStorage, keyed by the tutorial's address (see "Progress persistence" in question()), so this writes a small page, learnr2-restore.html, next to the rendered tutorial in the cache; opening it stores the answers under the tutorial's own address and forwards to the tutorial. Loading a file replaces whatever that browser had saved for the same tutorial. When this function's own server is stopped the page is deleted; if an already-running learnr2 server was used instead, it stays until the next load or re-render.

The same thing without R

Every tutorial page also has a Load Answers button beside Start Over, and accepts a dropped .json file anywhere on the page. It does in the browser what this function does from R, matching ids the same way, so a reader of a published copy of a tutorial (on GitHub Pages, say) can pick up a download without an R session. This function is for the student in a Codespace, where the tutorial must be rendered and served first, and for the "R Tutorials" VS Code extension's Load Answers File... command, which calls it.

See also

run_tutorial(), download_answers_button(), submission_time().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
load_tutorial("~/Downloads/orientation-2026-11-08T14-02-11-305Z.json")
} # }
